history.dynasty: Satavahana and Ikshvaku (inscriptions and coins); Mahatalavarasa coins also found
history.period: 1st century BCE to 3rd century CE (site active; possibly through 4th-5th century)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Phanigiri is an excavated Buddhist monastic site on a 150-200 ft double hillock north of Phanigiri village (Thirumalgiri mandal, Suryapet district), the name meaning 'hillock of snake hood' (Sanskrit phani = snake, giri = hillock). Preliminary excavation began in 1941 by Khaja Muhammad Ahmad of the Hyderabad state archaeology department; systematic excavations from the 1980s-2000s revealed a Maha Stupa, a stone-pillared congregation hall, three Viharas, two apsidal Chaityagrihas, sculptured panels with Jataka stories, and Brahmi label inscriptions of the Satavahana and Ikshvaku dynasties, plus coins of Mahatalavarasa, Satavahana and Ikshvaku kings and early historic material. In April 2019 archaeologists unearthed a rare life-sized (1.73 m) stucco Bodhisattva here; a Roman coin of Augustus points to ancient trade links. Thorana panels indicate the co-existence of Hinayana and Mahayana Buddhism - an important centre of both. In 2026 the Telangana heritage department earmarked Rs 1.6 crore for conservation/restoration at Phanigiri (with Gajulabanda). Some recovered artefacts are stored in a village panchayat house. CSV state 'Suryapet' corrected: Telangana. No published opening hours; treat as an open-air ASI/heritage site with daylight access - verify locally.

name: Phanigiri Buddhist Site
town_description: Phanigiri is a village in Thirumalgiri mandal of Suryapet district, Telangana, set amid plain farmlands dotted with rocky hillocks near the Krishna-Godavari delta network. The Buddhist site occupies the northern top of a large double hillock about 150-200 feet high on the northern side of the village, about 40 km north-northwest of Suryapet town and 80 km south-southwest of Warangal.

travel.road: About 40 km north-northwest of Suryapet via NH365B; about 110 km from Hyderabad
